paper.title: Toward an improved definition of a healthy microbiome for healthy aging.
paper.authors: Ghosh TS, Shanahan F, O'Toole PW.

steps.evidence: For samples belonging to these two repositories, the species-level and genus-level taxonomic profiles were obtained using metaphlan2 (ref. ).
For the ISC datasets, the pathway-level abundances were obtained using the humann2 pipeline
we used the single SPINGO classifier pipeline for profiling the taxonomy at both the genus and species levels.
all data were converted to both relative abundances as well as transformed to the centered-log-ratio (clr) transformation
The correlations were computed using corr.test function of the psych R package (version 2.1.9).

we first utilized robust linear regression models (function rlm of the MASS package version 7.3.54) to regress (or to predict) each of the different uniqueness measures with Shannon diversity as the predictor
The statistical significance of the fits or associations were computed using the two-sided robust F-test (performed using the f.robftest function of the sfsmisc package v 1.1.12 in R).
The adonis function of the vegan package version 2.5.7 was used for this purpose.
we specifically identified 107 species-level taxa that were commonly detected in at least 5% of the samples in at least 60% studies individually

P values of associations obtained using robust linear regression models were corrected separately for each of the five microbiome summary statistics (four measures of uniqueness and Shannon diversity), using the Benjamini–Hochberg correction to obtain the false discovery rate (FDR) (or Q-value) (computed using the p.adjust function with ‘method’ parameter = ‘fdr’ of the base R package version 4.1.0).
